current_example.worked_solution:
In general, $\text{rank}(\mathbf{T}) = \text{dim}(\text{Im}(\mathbf{T})) = \text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ -6 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 7 & 7 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{7}{4}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $2$ pivot columns, we have that 

$$
\textrm{rank}(\mathbf{T})=\textrm{rank}(T)=2.
$$
